hints: Focus on what changes as you go down Group 17 from Cl to Br to I, especially atomic size and bond strength.
The H-X bond gets longer and weaker from $\text{HCl}$ to $\text{HI}$, so think about what that means for stability.
Connect weaker bonds to easier decomposition and easier loss of electrons by the halide ion to decide which of 1, 2 and 3 truly increase.
walkthrough:
**Look at the atoms involved**

Think of the sequence $\text{HCl}$, $\text{HBr}$, $\text{HI}$. Hydrogen is the same each time, but the halogen gets bigger down the group: Cl < Br < I.

Trend in size:
$$\text{Cl} < \text{Br} < \text{I}$$

**Check bond length (statement 2)**

A bigger halogen atom means its outer orbital is larger and more diffuse, so overlap with hydrogen is poorer and the bond is longer.

Trend:
$$\text{H-Cl} < \text{H-Br} < \text{H-I in length}$$ 
So statement 2 increases and is true.

**Check thermal stability (statement 1)**

Longer bonds are weaker bonds because overlap is poorer. Bond enthalpies fall from $\text{HCl}$ to $\text{HI}$.

This means $\text{HI}$ decomposes to $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{I}_2$ on heating much more easily than $\text{HCl}$ does. So thermal stability decreases, not increases. Statement 1 is false.

**Check ease of oxidation (statement 3)**

Ease of oxidation means how easily $\text{X}^-$ loses electrons to form $\text{X}_2$. Larger ions like $\text{I}^-$ hold their outer electrons less tightly and are better reducing agents.

Trend in reducing power:
$$\text{Cl}^- < \text{Br}^- < \text{I}^-$$
So $\text{HI}$ is oxidised most easily, even by concentrated sulfuric acid, while $\text{HCl}$ is not. Statement 3 increases and is true.

**Combine the conclusions**

Only 2 and 3 increase, while 1 decreases. In the standard 1, 2, 3 combination key, 2 and 3 only corresponds to option C.

options.A: Incorrect. This option means 1, 2 and 3 all increase. Statements 2 and 3 do increase, but statement 1 is wrong because thermal stability decreases from $\text{HCl}$ to $\text{HI}$ as the H-X bond gets weaker.
options.B: Incorrect. This option means 1 and 2 only are correct. Bond length (2) is correct, but thermal stability (1) does not increase. $\text{HCl}$ is the most stable and $\text{HI}$ decomposes most readily.
options.C: Correct. Bond length (2) increases because the halogen atom gets larger, and ease of oxidation (3) increases because $\text{I}^-$ is a much stronger reducing agent than $\text{Br}^-$ and $\text{Cl}^-$. Thermal stability (1) decreases, so it is excluded.
options.D: Incorrect. This option means 1 only is correct. Thermal stability actually shows the opposite trend. It is highest for $\text{HCl}$ and lowest for $\text{HI}$ due to decreasing H-X bond strength.
